history.summary: Compact 527 sqft freehold '2BR' at Prime Residence (D14 Geylang/Aljunied) for $800k / $1518 PSF, right at the $1510 district median. Sub-$1M freehold entry near Aljunied MRT is attractive on price, but only 7 URA transactions make the 5.2%/yr rate unreliable and 527 sqft for a 2BR is very cramped — a Neutral on thin data and unit quality.
history.rating_rationale: Only 7 URA txn — the 5.2%/yr appreciation is statistically unreliable. PSF $1518 vs $1510 median is fair (not a discount). 527 sqft for a '2BR' is a small/compact layout (bedroom_sqft_mismatch), and the Aljunied/Geylang locale carries some stigma that caps owner-occupier appeal. The sub-$1M freehold price and broad rental demand keep it from Avoid, but thin data and cramped unit prevent a Buy.

history.summary: Small freehold Geylang unit priced essentially at market; the algo's 'cheap' read is contradicted by recent transactions, and reviews flag management/maintenance issues.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,518 psf is right on top of the project's recent-transaction average of ~$1,511 psf (range $1,507-1,514 in last 12 months) - so the -18.1% age-adjusted 'cheapness' is NOT borne out by actual comps; it is at market. The 527 sqft 'two-bed' triggers a bedroom_sqft_mismatch flag (this is effectively a compact 1BR-plus), and appreciation rests on only 7 transactions, too thin to trust. Freehold is not a forward edge per the backtest. Web reviews cite poor MCST management, mold and corridor odor. Location is decent (D14 Geylang/Mountbatten fringe, ~Aljunied/Dakota MRT) and the $800k quantum keeps it liquid, but with no real value undercut and no dated catalyst this is a hold-neutral, not a buy.

Thin evidence base - only 7 appreciation transactions in a 39-unit project
Negative reviews: poor MCST management, moldy walls, corridor odor
